S.source: printed p. 484; entry 'kna'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: in-i-nay shput mi-lhugqu, k-i-na ca-cuini m-usha
S.PHON: ininaj ʃput miɬuŋqu kina θaθuini muʃa
S.FORM: in-i-nay shput mi-lhungqu, k-i-na tha-thuini m-usha
S.PHON: ininaj ʃput miɬuŋqu kina θaθuini muʃa
S.TRANSL: That person was here and left just now

S.source: printed p. 484; entry 'kna'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: cicu k-i-na tilha itia uan i-nay
S.PHON: θiθu kina tiɬa itia uan inaj
S.FORM: thithu k-i-na tilha itia uan i-nay
S.PHON: θiθu kina tiɬa itia uan inaj
S.TRANSL: He was here until yesterday

S.source: printed p. 484; entry 'kna'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: yaku k-i-na ta shashanu mu-buhat k-u-na ca-cuini-an antu pa-pagqa
S.PHON: jaku kina ta ʃaʃanu mubuhat kuna θaθuinian antu papaŋqa
S.FORM: yaku k-i-na ta shashanu mu-buhat k-u-na tha-thuini-an antu pa-pangqa
S.PHON: jaku kina ta ʃaʃanu mubuhat kuna θaθuinian antu papaŋqa
S.TRANSL: I've been working from this morning until now without a break

S.source: printed p. 484; entry 'kna'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: haya wa ayuzi miarai-rain k-i-na ta shashanu k-u-na ma-humhum-an miarain ishqala
S.PHON: haja wa ajuði miarairain kina ta ʃaʃanu kuna mahumhuman miarain iʃqala
S.FORM: haya wa ayuzi miarai-rain k-i-na ta shashanu k-u-na ma-humhum-an miarain ishqala
S.PHON: haja βa ajuði miarairain kina ta ʃaʃanu kuna mahumhuman miarain iʃqala
S.TRANSL: That man is drunk from morning till nightfall

S.source: printed p. 484; entry 'kna'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: ita k-i-na ta shashanu i-nay mi-lhugqu, k-u-na ca-cuini-an miaqay i-nay mi-lhugqu
S.PHON: ita kina ta ʃaʃanu inaj miɬuŋqu kuna θaθuinian miaqaj inaj miɬuŋqu
S.FORM: ita k-i-na ta shashanu i-nay mi-lhungqu, k-u-na tha-thuini-an miaqay i-nay mi-lhungqu
S.PHON: ita kina ta ʃaʃanu inaj miɬuŋqu kuna θaθuinian miaqaj inaj miɬuŋqu

TRANSL.notes: Source note: remark made in mild complaint

S.TRANSL: We have been sitting here since this morning (and) are still sitting here

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kna' (opens on p. 484); sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–i–na'
S.FORM: k-i-na ta-tilha uan ita tu i-nay malh-ka-kakca
S.PHON: kina tatiɬa uan ita tu inaj maɬkakakθa
S.FORM: k-i-na ta-tilha uan ita tu i-nay malh-ka-kaktha
S.PHON: kina tatiɬa uan ita tu inaj maɬkakakθa
S.TRANSL: We have been discussing things here since yesterday (without leaving)

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kna' (opens on p. 484); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–u–na'
S.FORM: minu ihu qa k-u-na ca-cuini uan mu-nay. Maka uka shawa-shawan
S.PHON: minu ihu qa kuna θaθuini uan munaj maka uka ʃawaʃawan
S.FORM: minu ihu qa k-u-na tha-thuini uan mu-nay. Maka uka shawa-shawan
S.PHON: minu ihu qa kuna θaθuini uan munaj maka uka ʃaβaʃaβan
S.TRANSL: Why didn't you come until now? Because I had no free time

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kna' (opens on p. 484); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–u–na'
S.FORM: yamin tu kahiwan naur in-i-nay Barawbaw k-u-na ca-cuini-an
S.PHON: jamin tu kahiwan naur ininaj barawbaw kuna θaθuinian
S.FORM: yamin tu kahiwan naur in-i-nay Barawbaw k-u-na tha-thuini-an
S.PHON: jamin tu kahiβan naur ininaj barawbaw kuna θaθuinian
S.TRANSL: Since long ago until now we have been in Barawbaw

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kna' (opens on p. 484); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–u–na'
S.FORM: ti ama shashanu matin-humhum mu-buhat k-u-na ca-cuini-an miaqay i-say buhat mu-buhat
S.PHON: ti ama ʃaʃanu matinhumhum mubuhat kuna θaθuinian miaqaj isaj buhat mubuhat
S.FORM: ti ama shashanu matin-humhum mu-buhat k-u-na tha-thuini-an miaqay i-say buhat mu-buhat
S.PHON: ti ama ʃaʃanu matinhumhum mubuhat kuna θaθuinian miaqaj isaj buhat mubuhat
S.TRANSL: Father went to work in the fields early this morning and is still there working

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kna' (opens on p. 484); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–u–na'
S.FORM: a k-u-na sa simaq-in a m-usha
S.PHON: a kuna sa simaqin a muʃa
S.FORM: a k-u-na sa simaq-in a m-usha
S.PHON: a kuna sa simaqin a muʃa
S.TRANSL: We will leave tomorrow

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'kpiz'; sense 2; illustrates 'pig–kpiz–in'
S.FORM: numa suma pig-kpiz-in a k-ifa-k-ifaz ya ma-humhum, uka sa pinuqrum numa sa caw k-ifaz-an sa kpiz
S.PHON: numa suma piŋkpiðin a kifakifað ja mahumhum uka sa pinuqrum numa sa θaw kifaðan sa kpið
S.FORM: numa suma ping-kpiz-in a k-ifa-k-ifaz ya ma-humhum, uka sa pinuqrum numa sa thaw k-ifaz-an sa kpiz
S.PHON: numa suma piŋkpiðin a kiɸakiɸað ja mahumhum uka sa pinuqrum numa sa θaw kiɸaðan sa kpið
S.TRANSL: Then some were made into sleeping cloths to cover (them) up when it got dark-if they had no blanket the people covered up with a sleeping cloth

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'krasa'; illustrates 'krasa'
S.FORM: yaku ya qirqir-an sa krasa a min-ura iza
S.PHON: jaku ja qirqiran sa krasa a minura iða
S.FORM: yaku ya qirqir-an sa krasa a min-ura iza
S.PHON: jaku ja qirqiran sa krasa a minura iða
S.TRANSL: If I am stung by a yellow jacket I will pass out

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'ktalha'; illustrates 'ktalha'
S.FORM: ma-cuaw ma-qitan qaramat ya ktalha sa afu
S.PHON: maθuaw maqitan qaramat ja ktaɬa sa afu
S.FORM: ma-thuaw ma-qitan qaramat ya ktalha sa afu
S.PHON: maθuaw maqitan qaramat ja ktaɬa sa aɸu
S.TRANSL: The qaramat clam is very delicious when eaten with rice

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'ktalha'; sense 2; illustrates 'ktalhá–n'
S.FORM: yaku k-m-an sa afu ktalhá-n sa rusaw
S.PHON: jaku kman sa afu ktaɬan sa rusaw
S.FORM: yaku k-m-an sa afu ktalha-n sa rusaw
S.PHON: jaku kman sa aɸu ktaɬan sa rusaw
S.TRANSL: I'm eating fish with rice

S.source: printed p. 485; entry 'ktalha'; sense 3; illustrates 'k–un–talha'
S.FORM: numa isisuaiza ya a ma-kan iza pu-apaw-in caycuy k-un-talha, ma-cuaw ya k-un-talha sa kahum, ma-zima ya k-m-an
S.PHON: numa isisuaiða ja a makan iða puapawin θajθuj kuntaɬa maθuaw ja kuntaɬa sa kahum maðima ja kman
S.FORM: numa isisuaiza ya a ma-kan iza pu-apaw-in thaythuy k-un-talha, ma-thuaw ya k-un-talha sa kahum, ma-zima ya k-m-an
S.PHON: numa isisuaiða ja a makan iða puapaβin θajθuj kuntaɬa maθuaw ja kuntaɬa sa kahum maðima ja kman
S.TRANSL: Then when it was ready to be eaten they took it out and ate it as a side dish (and) many people ate the deerskin (because) it was delicious

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktalha' (opens on p. 485); sense 3; illustrates 'k–un–talha'
S.FORM: yaku ya antu k-un-talha sa pania'an antu ma-zima sa afu
S.PHON: jaku ja antu kuntaɬa sa paniaʔan antu maðima sa afu
S.FORM: yaku ya antu k-un-talha sa pania'an antu ma-zima sa afu
S.PHON: jaku ja antu kuntaɬa sa paniaʔan antu maðima sa aɸu
S.TRANSL: I don't like rice without a side dish of vegetables

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktalha' (opens on p. 485); sense 3; illustrates 'k–un–talha'
S.FORM: ita ya k-un-talha sa aqtalha palha-na-suhúy uan ma-qasbit
S.PHON: ita ja kuntaɬa sa aqtaɬa paɬanasuhuj uan maqasbit
S.FORM: ita ya k-un-talha sa aqtalha palha-na-suhuy uan ma-qasbit
S.PHON: ita ja kuntaɬa sa aqtaɬa paɬanasuhuj uan maqasbit
S.TRANSL: When we eat pork just dip it there in the soy sauce

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 2; illustrates 'k–in–tir–in'
S.TRANSL: The mother pinched her child

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 3; illustrates 'k–m–in–tir'
S.TRANSL: The mother pinched her child

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 5; illustrates 'kti–ktir–i'
S.FORM: kti-ktir-i uan nak a rikus maqa mig-kashlay
S.PHON: ktiktiri uan nak a rikus maqa miŋkaʃlaj
S.FORM: kti-ktir-i uan nak a rikus maqa ming-kashlay
S.PHON: ktiktiri uan nak a rikus maqa miŋkaʃlaj
S.TRANSL: Please massage my back because it's numb/aching

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 6; illustrates 'kti–ktir–in'
S.FORM: haya ayuzi ma-cuaw kti-ktir-in cicu a binanau'az maqa antu t-un-maza cicu a lalawa
S.PHON: haja ajuði maθuaw ktiktirin θiθu a binanauʔað maqa antu tunmaða θiθu a lalawa
S.FORM: haya ayuzi ma-thuaw kti-ktir-in thithu a binanau'az maqa antu t-un-maza thithu a lalawa
S.PHON: haja ajuði maθuaw ktiktirin θiθu a binanauʔað maqa antu tunmaða θiθu a lalaβa
S.TRANSL: That man's wife pinches him a lot because he doesn't listen to her

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 8; illustrates 'ktir–i'
S.FORM: i-zaháy a binanau'az ktir-i ihu pia-kashpar a maqa ma-qiaqia
S.PHON: iðahaj a binanauʔað ktiri ihu piakaʃpar a maqa maqiaqia
S.FORM: i-zahay a binanau'az ktir-i ihu pia-kashpar a maqa ma-qiaqia
S.PHON: iðahaj a binanauʔað ktiri ihu piakaʃpar a maqa maqiaqia
S.TRANSL: Pinch that woman hard so that she squeals

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 9; illustrates 'ktir–ik'
S.FORM: cicu mu-muqmuq malhinuna, a ktir-ik maqa a pagqa
S.PHON: θiθu mumuqmuq maɬinuna a ktirik maqa a paŋqa
S.FORM: thithu mu-muqmuq malhinuna, a ktir-ik maqa a pangqa
S.PHON: θiθu mumuqmuq maɬinuna a ktirik maqa a paŋqa
S.TRANSL: He was talking nonsense (so) I pinched him to make him stop

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 10; illustrates 'ktir–in'
S.TRANSL: The child's mother is pinching him (in punishment)

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 11; illustrates 'k–un–ti–ktir'
S.TRANSL: My wife keeps pinching me (repeatedly)

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 12; illustrates 'k–un–tir'
S.TRANSL: The mother pinched/is pinching her child

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 12; illustrates 'k–un–tir'
S.TRANSL: The mother will pinch her child

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 12; illustrates 'k–un–tir'
S.FORM: tima sa k-un-tir nak a patuk?
S.PHON: tima sa kuntir nak a patuk
S.FORM: tima sa k-un-tir nak a patuk?
S.PHON: tima sa kuntir nak a patuk
S.TRANSL: Who pinched my cheek?

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 12; illustrates 'k–un–tir'
S.FORM: nak a binanau'az k-un-tir yakin, numa yaku mukcuaw, "minu qa a k-un-tir yakin?"
S.PHON: nak a binanauʔað kuntir jakin numa jaku mukθuaw minu qa a kuntir jakin
S.FORM: nak a binanau'az k-un-tir yakin, numa yaku mukthuaw, "minu qa a k-un-tir yakin?"
S.PHON: nak a binanauʔað kuntir jakin numa jaku mukθuaw minu qa a kuntir jakin
S.TRANSL: My wife pinched me so I was startled (and said) "Why did you pinch me?"

S.source: printed p. 486; entry 'ktir'; sense 13; illustrates 'lhig–ktir–in'
S.FORM: nak a paqi lhig-ktir-in nak a binanau'az
S.PHON: nak a paqi ɬiŋktirin nak a binanauʔað
S.FORM: nak a paqi lhing-ktir-in nak a binanau'az
S.PHON: nak a paqi ɬiŋktirin nak a binanauʔað
S.TRANSL: My wife pinched my buttock

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktir' (opens on p. 486); sense 15; illustrates 'lh–ktir'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: as to discipline a child

S.TRANSL: Pinch his/her cheek!'

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktir' (opens on p. 486); sense 16; illustrates 'lh–ktir–ik'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: mother to a disobeying child

S.TRANSL: I will pinch your cheek

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktir' (opens on p. 486); sense 17; illustrates 'lh–ktir–in'
S.TRANSL: A woman pinched my buttock

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; illustrates 'ktun'; reading 1 of 2 of 'ktun (ihu) i–zaháy a klhiw'

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; illustrates 'ktun'

S.TRANSL: I was cutting the rope

TRANSL.notes: Source note: but am not doing it now

S.TRANSL: I was cutting the rope

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 6; illustrates 'ktun–i'
S.TRANSL: Don't cut the rope!

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 6; illustrates 'ktun–i'
S.TRANSL: Don't cut the rope!

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 7; illustrates 'ktun–ik'
S.TRANSL: I cut the rope

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 8; illustrates 'kug–ktu–ktun'
S.FORM: i-zaháy a caw kug-ktu-ktun tuqris a klhiw
S.PHON: iðahaj a θaw kuŋktuktun tuqris a kɬiw
S.FORM: i-zahay a thaw kung-ktu-ktun tuqris a klhiw
S.PHON: iðahaj a θaw kuŋktuktun tuqris a kɬiw
S.TRANSL: That person is always cutting the tension cords of other people's spring traps

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 9; illustrates 'k–un–tun'
S.TRANSL: She cut the umbilical cord

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 9; illustrates 'k–un–tun'
S.TRANSL: I'm cutting a rope

S.source: printed p. 487; entry 'ktun'; sense 10; illustrates 'pish–ktun'
S.TRANSL: Why did that rope break?

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kuaz'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kag–kuaz–in'
S.TRANSL: The buffalo demolished the embankment between the fields by trampling on it

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kuaz'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mug–kuaz'; reading 1 of 2 of 'haya (wa) saran maqa miarain qusaz–in numa mug–kuaz'
S.FORM: haya saran maqa miarain qusaz-in numa mug-kuaz
S.PHON: haja saran maqa miarain qusaðin numa muŋkuað
S.FORM: haya saran maqa miarain qusaz-in numa mung-kuaz
S.PHON: haja saran maqa miarain qusaðin numa muŋkuað
S.TRANSL: The road was washed out because of heavy rains

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kuaz'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mug–kuaz'; reading 2 of 2 of 'haya (wa) saran maqa miarain qusaz–in numa mug–kuaz'
S.FORM: haya wa saran maqa miarain qusaz-in numa mug-kuaz
S.PHON: haja wa saran maqa miarain qusaðin numa muŋkuað
S.FORM: haya wa saran maqa miarain qusaz-in numa mung-kuaz
S.PHON: haja βa saran maqa miarain qusaðin numa muŋkuað
S.TRANSL: The road was washed out because of heavy rains

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kuaz'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'p–in–u–kuaz'
S.FORM: haya hudun maqa miarain qusaz-in ma-cuaw ma-ra'in a p-in-u-kuaz
S.PHON: haja hudun maqa miarain qusaðin maθuaw maraʔin a pinukuað
S.FORM: haya hudun maqa miarain qusaz-in ma-thuaw ma-ra'in a p-in-u-kuaz
S.PHON: haja hudun maqa miarain qusaðin maθuaw maraʔin a pinukuað
S.TRANSL: Because it rained a lot that mountain has developed a lot of landslides

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kuaz'; sense 8; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pu–kuaz–in'
S.FORM: haya wa buhat a rusun pu-kuaz-in i-zay a caw
S.PHON: haja wa buhat a rusun pukuaðin iðaj a θaw
S.FORM: haya wa buhat a rusun pu-kuaz-in i-zay a thaw
S.PHON: haja βa buhat a rusun pukuaðin iðaj a θaw
S.TRANSL: That person destroyed the earthen embankments between the fields (as with a hoe)

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kucu'; sense 2; illustrates 'kit–kucu–n'
S.TRANSL: You have lice in your hair

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kucu'; sense 2; illustrates 'kit–kucu–n'
S.TRANSL: I have lice in my hair

S.source: printed p. 488; entry 'kucun'; sense 3; illustrates 'pug–kucun'
S.FORM: huya wa shput p-usha sa lhalhuzu pug-kucun
S.PHON: huja wa ʃput puʃa sa ɬaɬuðu puŋkuθun
S.FORM: huya wa shput p-usha sa lhalhuzu pung-kuthun
S.PHON: huja βa ʃput puʃa sa ɬaɬuðu puŋkuθun
S.TRANSL: That man is putting out a long string of traps to catch shrimp

S.source: printed p. 489; entry 'kudada(h)'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kudadah–ik'
S.TRANSL: I took the pen apart

S.source: printed p. 489; entry 'kudush'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kudush–kudush'
S.FORM: numa sa i-zay a caw i-fafaw mi-lhugqu kudush-kudush, min-daq sh-humhum-an
S.PHON: numa sa iðaj a θaw ifafaw miɬuŋqu kuduʃkuduʃ mindaq ʃhumhuman
S.FORM: numa sa i-zay a thaw i-fafaw mi-lhungqu kudush-kudush, min-daq sh-humhum-an
S.PHON: numa sa iðaj a θaw iɸaɸaw miɬuŋqu kuduʃkuduʃ mindaq ʃhumhuman
S.TRANSL: Then the man sat nervously on top (of a tree), for a long time until it got dark

S.source: printed p. 489; entry 'kufulh'; sense 2; illustrates 'k–m–ufulh'
S.TRANSL: Put sword grass thatch on the roof

S.source: printed p. 489; entry 'kufulh'; sense 2; illustrates 'k–m–ufulh'
S.FORM: ya k-m-ufulh sa taun pasay-in lhimza k-m-ufulh, numa ya mu-kaktun iza k-m-ufulh man-shirshir a tafuq pasay-in kakanan a qaulh qpit-in, numa ya q-im-pit iza maqa mashash-anak sa lhimza, numa pimpin-an
S.PHON: ja kmufuɬ sa taun pasajin ɬimða kmufuɬ numa ja mukaktun iða kmufuɬ manʃirʃir a tafuq pasajin kakanan a qauɬ qpitin numa ja qimpit iða maqa maʃaʃanak sa ɬimða numa pimpinan
S.FORM: ya k-m-ufulh sa taun pasay-in lhimza k-m-ufulh, numa ya mu-kaktun iza k-m-ufulh man-shirshir a tafuq pasay-in kakanan a qaulh qpit-in, numa ya q-im-pit iza maqa mashash-anak sa lhimza, numa pimpin-an
S.PHON: ja kmuɸuɬ sa taun pasajin ɬimða kmuɸuɬ numa ja mukaktun iða kmuɸuɬ manʃirʃir a taɸuq pasajin kakanan a qauɬ qpitin numa ja qimpit iða maqa maʃaʃanak sa ɬimða numa pimpinan
S.TRANSL: When we roof a house we use sword grass, and when we are done covering the roof we go along the edge using a bamboo pole to pinch the thatch (and) when it is pinched together we trim the ragged ends to make them even

S.source: printed p. 489; entry 'kufulh'; sense 3; illustrates 'kufulh–an'
S.FORM: nak a taun maqa niwan tu u-kaktun-in, niwan tu kufulh-an
S.PHON: nak a taun maqa niwan tu ukaktunin niwan tu kufuɬan
S.FORM: nak a taun maqa niwan tu u-kaktun-in, niwan tu kufulh-an
S.PHON: nak a taun maqa niβan tu ukaktunin niβan tu kuɸuɬan
S.TRANSL: Since my house isn't finished yet, it doesn't yet have a roof
